column5: fact   (ALL DEVICE, INVENTORY, CASE AND VAC FACTS BELOW ARE FICTIONAL DEMO DATA)
Device: CardioSeal TAVR System (fictional demo product), a transcatheter aortic valve replacement system. Sizes: 23 mm, 26 mm, 29 mm. Delivered via transfemoral access.

Cleared/approved indication: patients with symptomatic severe native aortic stenosis who are determined by a heart team to be at intermediate or high surgical risk. Use in low-risk patients, bicuspid valves or valve-in-valve is outside the current labeling.

The rep may support device preparation, answer IFU-based technical questions and confirm sizing charts. The rep may not give medical advice, select patients, direct clinical decisions, touch the sterile field or advise on anything outside the IFU.
Proctoring policy: a new operator needs a company proctor present for the first 10 cases. Cases 11-20: proctor available on request. After 20 cases the operator is independent.

Off-label or clinical-use questions go to the Clinical Affairs team (clinical.affairs@example.com, fictional). Device malfunctions, patient injuries or complaints must be reported per the complaint-handling SOP within 24 hours (complaints line 1-800-000-0200, fictional). Contract and pricing questions go to the Hospital Contracts Manager.

Clinical evidence (fictional): 30-day all-cause mortality 1.9% and disabling stroke 1.4% in the intermediate-risk registry of 2,100 patients. Economic evidence (fictional): average length of stay reduced by 1.6 days versus surgical AVR; estimated net hospital cost saving of $4,200 per case at 6 months.

Typical VAC members and what they care about: Chief of Cardiology (clinical outcomes, operator training), Supply Chain Director (price, consignment terms, standardization), CFO delegate (cost per case, length of stay), Nurse Director cath lab (setup time, staff training), Biomedical/Imaging lead (imaging compatibility).

Demo status: interventional cardiologist. 7 TAVR cases completed with CardioSeal; proctoring threshold 10 cases, so a proctor should be present. Next case scheduled this Thursday at 07:30. Prefers 26 mm and 29 mm sizes available plus a pre-dilation balloon set. Inventory at the hospital: 23 mm x1, 26 mm x2, 29 mm x0. Consignment count NOT yet confirmed for this week.

Demo status: structural heart cardiologist. 24 TAVR cases completed; independent operator. Next case Friday 10:00. Prefers 23 mm and 26 mm sizes. Inventory: 23 mm x2, 26 mm x3, 29 mm x1. Consignment confirmed Monday. Imaging suite set up with new C-arm; she asked for cath lab staff refresher on delivery system.

Demo status: new operator, 2 TAVR cases completed, proctoring threshold 10 cases. Next case in 9 days; proctor not yet scheduled. Asked about sizing for a borderline annulus and was referred to the sizing chart in the IFU. Inventory: 26 mm x1 only.

Demo status: electrophysiologist, 12 cases completed (proctor available on request). Interested in extending use beyond current labeling in his lower-risk patients; reminder that this is off-label and must be routed to Clinical Affairs.

Demo VAC status: CardioSeal under VAC review; evidence package submitted last month. Next VAC meeting in 12 days. Supply Chain Director asked for consignment terms and a price comparison; CFO delegate asked for cost-per-case and length-of-stay data. Cath lab consignment: 23 mm x3, 26 mm x4, 29 mm x2, last counted 5 days ago.

Demo VAC status: product approved by VAC last quarter; standardization agreement signed. Next VAC meeting not scheduled. Nurse Director asked for a cath lab staff training session. Consignment: 23 mm x1, 26 mm x2, 29 mm x1, count overdue by 3 weeks.
